QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_25

question.text: What does a 'normal' or positively sloped yield curve indicate?

answer.text: Long-term rates are lower than short-term rates
Long-term rates are higher than short-term rates
All rates are the same regardless of maturity

explanation.text: The Logic: A normal (positive) yield curve indicates higher yield for higher maturity, so long-term yields are above short-term yields. The Trap: An inverted yield curve (long-term below short-term) may indicate worsening economic or recessionary conditions, while a flat curve means rates are similar across maturities. Note: The shape of the yield curve is interpreted with caution and is one of several inputs in assessing economic conditions.
